steps.title: Sermons — list, linked sermons, edit, player, delete
steps.goal: Under `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons` a leader with `sermons.link` lists sermons (members see published rows; any `sermons.*` holder also sees drafts and scheduled rows, with status/kind/search filters), creates a linked sermon on the Link tab of `/sermons/new` with a live `parseMediaLink` preview (YouTube nocookie iframe, Google Drive preview, Dropbox/other https native stream, or 'opens at provider'), edits title/speaker/preached_on/series/scripture_refs/description and the publish state (now, scheduled in the org timezone, or draft) on `/sermons/[id]`, plays any kind through `SermonPlayer` (uploaded media via a 1-hour signed URL re-minted on error, so 3.3b and 3.4 reuse it), and deletes with `sermons.delete` (DB trigger queues the file, share links cascade). Upload tab is a disabled placeholder for 3.3b; the share-links card is a placeholder for 3.4. All reads/writes use the user client under RLS; the service client is not imported.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 3.3a "Sermons — list, linked sermons, edit, player, delete" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §6 (Storage & media: buckets, signed URLs, `parseMediaLink`), §7 (CRUD through the user client, Server Actions), §8 (`(org)` route map) and §12 (Web verification), and `docs/DESIGN.md` §6 (the `sermons` rows of the policy table), §7 (bucket table, "External links" paragraph — authoritative for provider behaviour), §8 and §9 before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one — uploads (`ResumableUpload`, tus) are step 3.3b and share links are step 3.4.

## Goal
When you finish, a church leader holding `sermons.link` can open `/o/<slug>/sermons`, see every published sermon (and drafts/scheduled sermons if they hold any `sermons.*` permission), open `/o/<slug>/sermons/new`, paste a YouTube, Dropbox, Google Drive or other https link on the **Link** tab, see a live preview produced by `parseMediaLink`, save it as a draft or publish it, then open `/o/<slug>/sermons/<id>` to edit title, speaker, preached-on date, series, scripture references, description and publish state, watch or listen through `SermonPlayer`, and — with `sermons.delete` — delete it. `SermonPlayer` already plays **uploaded** sermons too (1-hour signed URL, re-minted on error) so that step 3.3b only has to add the upload path and step 3.4 can reuse the player on the public share page. The **Upload** tab exists as a disabled placeholder ("Uploads arrive in step 3.3b"). Every read goes through the user-scoped Supabase client under RLS; nothing in this step imports the service client.

## Inputs / prior state
- Step 3.1 built the org shell and guards. Reuse them exactly, never reshape them: `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` (`requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext = {org: {orgId, slug, name, status}, membershipStatus, personId, householdId, permissions: PermissionKey[], isSuperAdmin}`, `requirePerm(ctx, perm)`, `requireWritable(ctx)` throwing `organization_suspended`, `isWritable(ctx)`), `src/features/org/nav.ts` (`NAV_ITEMS`), `src/features/org/org-context.tsx`, `StatusBanner`, `src/lib/storage/signed-url.ts` (`getSignedUrl(bucket, path, expiresIn)` on the user client), `src/lib/actions/result.ts` (`ActionResult<T>`, `ok`, `fail`), `src/lib/supabase/errors.ts` (`toActionError`), `src/lib/env.ts` (`publicEnv()`, `serverEnv()`), `src/lib/supabase/{server,client}.ts` (`createServerSupabase()`, `createBrowserSupabase()`), the 2.1a Vitest harness (`vitest.config.ts`, `src/test/setup.ts` mocking `next/headers` and `next/navigation`), shadcn components in `src/components/ui/*`, and the settings query `getSettings(orgId)` (for `timezone`). Read `HANDOFF.md` "Deviations from plan" first — it records whether the guards use `forbidden()`/`notFound()` and the query module names 1.7a chose.
- Steps 1.6a/1.6b (`@church/domain`): `parseMediaLink(url, 'web' | 'mobile')` → `{ ok: true, kind, externalId?, canonicalUrl, embedUrl?, streamUrl?, strategy: 'youtube_hosted_embed' | 'native_stream' | 'webview' | 'open_external' } | { ok: false, reason: 'not_https' | 'invalid_url' | 'too_long' }`; `BUCKETS['sermon-media']` (`allowedMimeTypes`, `fileSizeLimitBytes`); `SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS` (3600), `SIGNED_URL_CACHE_MS`; `schemas/sermon.ts` — `sermonDetailsSchema` (`title` 1–200, `speaker`, `preached_on`, `series`, `scripture_refs` string[], `description` ≤ 4000, `publish_at` nullable datetime) and `sermonLinkSchema` (`external_url` https, refined with `parseMediaLink(url,'web').ok`); `errors.ts` (`toDomainError`, `errorMessageFor`, `DomainError`); `dates.ts` (org-timezone formatting helpers). Do not write a `z.object` for sermons in `apps/web` — import these.
- Step 1.7a (`@church/db`): `queries/sermons.ts` — `listSermons(orgId, { drafts, query, limit, offset })`, `getSermon(id)`, `insertSermonDraft(db, { id, org_id, title, …, media_kind, storage_path | external_url, external_id })` (the CALLER supplies `id`), `updateSermonAfterUpload`, `updateSermonDetails`, `publishSermon(id, publishAt)`, `deleteSermon(id)`; `queries/storage.ts` — `createSignedUrl(db, bucket, path, { ttl, download? })`; `keys.ts` — `queryKeys.sermons.list(orgId, filters)`, `.sermons.detail(id)`. Read the real signatures in `packages/db/src/queries/sermons.ts` before calling them; if one differs from this list, use the real one and note it.
- Database (`supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`, frozen if the HANDOFF ledger has a paste date — never edit it): `sermons` columns `id, org_id, title, speaker, preached_on, series, scripture_refs, description, media_kind (upload | youtube | dropbox | google_drive | url), storage_path, mime_type, file_size_bytes, duration_seconds, external_url, external_id, publish_at, created_by, updated_by`; checks `sermons_media_shape` (upload ⇒ `storage_path` set and `external_url` null; otherwise the reverse), `sermons_external_https` (`^https://`, ≤ 2048), `sermons_storage_path`. `publish_at null` = draft; `publish_at > now()` = scheduled. Policies (DESIGN §6): `ca_sermons_select_members` — members see `publish_at <= now()` rows, holders of any `sermons.*` permission see all rows of their org; `ca_sermons_insert_by_kind` — `media_kind = 'upload'` needs `sermons.upload`, every other kind needs `sermons.link`; update uses the same split; delete needs `sermons.delete`; every write also requires `app.org_writable(org_id)`. The delete trigger (`app.enqueue_storage_deletion`) queues the storage object into `storage_deletions`, `sermon_share_links` rows cascade, and `audit_log` records the delete. Storage: bucket `sermon-media`, private; `ca_storage_select` allows reading an object iff the sermon row is visible to the caller (`app.can_read_object`).
- Founder decisions that apply (HANDOFF "Founder answers"): decision 10 — Supabase Free, so `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` defaults to 50 and "link your own recording" is the lever for long recordings (surface that in the Link tab's helper text); decision 5 concerns share links and is step 3.4 — do not build the share panel here, leave the slot.

## Build
1. **Navigation and routing.** In `src/features/org/nav.ts` add (or un-comment) `Sermons` → `/o/<slug>/sermons`, visible to every active member (members read published sermons). Create the route files under `apps/web/app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/`: `page.tsx` (list), `loading.tsx`, `new/page.tsx`, `[id]/page.tsx`, `[id]/loading.tsx`, `[id]/not-found.tsx`. `params` and `searchParams` are Promises in Next 16 — `await` them. Every page starts with `const ctx = await requireOrgMember(orgSlug)`; write-capable UI is rendered only when `ctx.permissions` contains the relevant key, and every Server Action re-checks with `requirePerm` (UI gating is convenience, RLS + the guard are the security boundary).
2. **Permission helpers for this feature** in `src/features/sermons/perms.ts`: `canManageSermons(ctx)` = holds `sermons.upload` or `sermons.link` or `sermons.delete` (may see drafts, mirrors the select policy); `canEditSermon(ctx, sermon)` = `sermons.upload` when `media_kind === 'upload'`, else `sermons.link` (mirrors the update split); `canDeleteSermon(ctx)` = `sermons.delete`; `canCreateLink(ctx)` = `sermons.link`; `canCreateUpload(ctx)` = `sermons.upload`. Unit-test them with a table.
3. **List page** `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons` (`src/features/sermons/SermonsTable.tsx`, `SermonFilters.tsx`): read `searchParams` `status` (`published` default for members; `all` default for managers; also `drafts`, `scheduled`), `q` (title/speaker search), `kind` (`upload | youtube | dropbox | google_drive | url`), `page` (25 per page). Call `listSermons(ctx.org.orgId, …)` with the user client; if the 1.7a signature lacks `kind`/`status` filters, filter the page in TypeScript and note it — do not change `@church/db` beyond an additive parameter. Columns: title (link to `/sermons/<id>`), speaker, preached on (formatted with `dates.ts` in the org `timezone` from `getSettings`), a kind badge (Upload / YouTube / Dropbox / Google Drive / Link), status badge (Draft / Scheduled <local date-time> / Published), duration or file size when known. Header button "New sermon" when `canCreateLink(ctx) || canCreateUpload(ctx)`. Empty states: "No sermons yet" (+ the button when allowed); "Nothing matches these filters". Members never see the status filter (they can only see published rows anyway).
4. **New sermon page** `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/new` with shadcn `Tabs` **Upload | Link** (`src/features/sermons/NewSermonTabs.tsx`). The Upload tab is rendered disabled with the text "Uploads arrive in step 3.3b — until then, link a recording hosted on YouTube (unlisted), Dropbox or Google Drive." and is shown only when `canCreateUpload(ctx)`. The Link tab is shown only when `canCreateLink(ctx)`; if the visitor holds neither permission the page calls the 3.1 forbidden path (`forbidden()` or `notFound()` per HANDOFF). Default the selected tab to the one the visitor may use.
5. **`SermonForm`** (`src/features/sermons/SermonForm.tsx`, client, RHF + `zodResolver(sermonDetailsSchema)`): fields `title` (required), `speaker`, `preached_on` (date input), `series`, `scripture_refs` (comma-separated input mapped to `string[]`, trimmed, empties dropped), `description` (textarea), and a **Publish** control with three states: "Publish now", "Schedule for <datetime-local in the org timezone>", "Save as draft" → `publish_at` = now / the chosen instant converted with `dates.ts` / `null`. Reused by the Link tab and by the edit page (`mode: 'create' | 'edit'`). Inline field errors from Zod; the action's `ActionResult` error shown via `sonner` and, when `error.field` is set, attached to the field.
6. **`LinkPreview`** (`src/features/sermons/LinkPreview.tsx`, client): the Link tab has an `external_url` input; on change (debounced 300 ms) run `parseMediaLink(url, 'web')` in the browser. Render: `ok: false` → "Enter an https:// link" / "That does not look like a link" / "Link too long"; `youtube` → `<iframe src={embedUrl}>` (the `youtube-nocookie.com/embed/<id>` URL from the parser), `title="YouTube preview"`, `allow="encrypted-media; picture-in-picture; fullscreen"`, `referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"`, plus helper text "Unlisted videos work; private videos and videos with embedding disabled do not."; `google_drive` → `<iframe src={embedUrl}>` (Drive `/file/d/<id>/preview`) with helper "The file must be shared as 'Anyone with the link'."; `dropbox` with `strategy 'native_stream'` → `<audio controls src={streamUrl}>` (or `<video>` for `.mp4/.m4v`) with helper "Dropbox Basic accounts stop serving links after 20 GB per day."; any kind with `strategy 'open_external'` → "This link will open at the provider; it cannot be played inside the app." with the canonical URL. Never call the provider from the server (no oEmbed in Phase 1; "Re-check link" is step 5.7). Show the detected provider and `canonicalUrl`.
7. **Server Actions** in `src/features/sermons/actions.ts` (`'use server'`; each: `requireOrgMember(slug)` → `requirePerm` → `requireWritable(ctx)` → Zod parse with the `@church/domain` schema → `@church/db` query with the **user** client → `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/sermons')` and the detail path → `ActionResult` via `ok`/`fail(toActionError)`):
   - `createLinkedSermon(slug, input)`: `requirePerm(ctx, 'sermons.link')`; parse `sermonLinkSchema.extend`-free — parse `sermonDetailsSchema` and `sermonLinkSchema` separately; re-run `parseMediaLink(external_url, 'web')` on the server (never trust the client's parse) and reject `ok: false` with key `invalid_media_link`; `id = crypto.randomUUID()`; `insertSermonDraft(db, { id, org_id: ctx.org.orgId, media_kind: parsed.kind, external_url: parsed.canonicalUrl, external_id: parsed.externalId ?? null, title, speaker, preached_on, series, scripture_refs, description })`; then `publishSermon(db, id, publish_at)` when the form chose publish/schedule; return `{ id }`; the client redirects to `/o/<slug>/sermons/<id>`. A 42501 from the insert (e.g. `sermons.link` revoked meanwhile) maps to `permission_denied` through `toActionError`.
   - `updateSermon(slug, id, input)`: load the row with `getSermon(id)` (404 if missing), `requirePerm(ctx, canEditSermon-key)`, parse `sermonDetailsSchema`, `updateSermonDetails(db, id, patch)`; `publish_at` changes go through `publishSermon(db, id, publishAt | null)` so "Unpublish (back to draft)" is possible. For linked sermons also accept a changed `external_url` (re-parse, update `media_kind`/`external_url`/`external_id` together so `sermons_media_shape` holds); a linked sermon can never become an upload or vice versa — reject with `invalid_payload`.
   - `deleteSermonAction(slug, id)`: `requirePerm(ctx, 'sermons.delete')`; `deleteSermon(db, id)`; `redirect` to the list with a toast flag. The DB trigger queues the file for deletion; the UI text says "The recording file is removed by the housekeeping job (step 3.6); share links for this sermon stop working immediately."
   - `mintSermonMediaUrl(slug, id)`: `requireOrgMember` only (any member who can see the row may play it — RLS on `storage.objects` decides); `getSermon(id)`; if `media_kind !== 'upload'` return `invalid_payload`; `getSignedUrl('sermon-media', storage_path, SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS)` → `{ url, expiresAt }`. Used by the player to re-mint.
8. **Detail / edit page** `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/[id]`: `getSermon(id)` with the user client → `notFound()` when null (RLS hides other orgs' rows and drafts from plain members — a 404, never a 403, so existence is not leaked). Layout: header (title, status badge, kind badge), `SermonPlayer` (item 9), `SermonForm` in edit mode when `canEditSermon(ctx, sermon)` else a read-only details card, a "Share links" card placeholder with the single line "Share links arrive in step 3.4" (only for `sermons.link`/`sermons.upload` holders — 3.4 replaces this card with `ShareLinksPanel`), and a danger zone with `DeleteSermonButton` (`AlertDialog` confirm naming the consequences) when `canDeleteSermon(ctx)`. For an **upload** row whose `file_size_bytes` is null and `publish_at` is null, show an "Upload incomplete" notice instead of the player (3.3b adds the resume flow here) — do not build resume now.
9. **`SermonPlayer`** (`src/features/sermons/SermonPlayer.tsx`, client) with props `{ sermon: { id, media_kind, external_url, external_id, mime_type }, media?: { url, expiresAt } , onRemint?: () => Promise<{ url, expiresAt } | null>, variant: 'admin' | 'share' }`. Strategy per `parseMediaLink(external_url, 'web')` for external kinds: `youtube` → `<iframe src={embedUrl}>` (`youtube-nocookie`), `allow="autoplay; encrypted-media; picture-in-picture; fullscreen"`, `allowFullScreen`, `referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"`, 16:9 box; `google_drive` → `<iframe src={embedUrl}>` (preview); `native_stream` → `<audio controls preload="metadata">` for audio MIME/extensions, `<video controls playsInline>` for video, `src={streamUrl}`; `open_external` → a prominent "Open at <provider>" link (`target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Always render a secondary "Open at provider" link under external players (helps when embeds fail). For `upload`: the server page mints `media` with `getSignedUrl('sermon-media', storage_path, SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS)` and passes it; the client renders `<audio>`/`<video>` by `mime_type`; on the element's `error` event, or when `Date.now() > expiresAt - 60_000` at play time, call `onRemint()` (the `mintSermonMediaUrl` action, bound in the page) exactly once and reload `src` preserving `currentTime`; if it fails show "Could not load the recording — reload the page." Put the strategy dispatch in a pure helper `src/features/sermons/player-strategy.ts` (`playerPlanFor(sermon): { kind: 'iframe', src } | { kind: 'audio' | 'video', src } | { kind: 'external', href, provider } | { kind: 'signed_upload' }`) and unit-test it with the parser's own cases. Step 3.4 imports `SermonPlayer` with `variant: 'share'` and step 4.2 mirrors `player-strategy.ts` on mobile — keep it free of Next-specific imports.
10. **Dates and timezone.** Format `preached_on` (a date, no timezone shift) and `publish_at` (an instant, shown in the org timezone from `getSettings`) with `@church/domain` `dates.ts`; convert the `datetime-local` schedule value to an ISO instant with the org timezone, not the browser's. Put the two conversions in `src/features/sermons/dates.ts` with tests (a DST boundary and a year boundary).
11. **Tests** (2.1a harness): `perms.test.ts`, `player-strategy.test.ts` (one row per provider/strategy incl. `open_external` and upload), `dates.test.ts`, `actions.test.ts` with a mocked user client — `createLinkedSermon` rejects a non-https URL with `invalid_media_link` before touching the DB, passes the parser's `canonicalUrl`/`kind`/`externalId` to `insertSermonDraft`, calls `publishSermon` only when publishing, maps a `42501` PostgREST error to `permission_denied`; `updateSermon` refuses to change an upload into a link (`invalid_payload`); `deleteSermonAction` requires `sermons.delete`. A thin `LinkPreview.test.tsx` (jsdom) asserting the YouTube branch renders an iframe pointing at `youtube-nocookie.com` and the http branch renders the "Enter an https:// link" message.
12. **Copy and help text**: Link tab helper at the top: "Recordings longer than the upload limit (currently <NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB> MB) are best hosted as an unlisted YouTube video, in Dropbox or in Google Drive and linked here." — read the number from `publicEnv()` (add `maxUploadMb` there via `readMaxUploadMb(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB)` if 2.1a did not expose it; keep the literal `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` reference so Next inlines it).

## Constraints
- Reads and writes use the user-scoped client only; `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` stays un-imported by this feature. No elevated key ever reaches the browser.
- Do not add Zod schemas, media parsing or path builders to `apps/web` — import from `@church/domain`; do not duplicate query code — extend `@church/db/queries/sermons.ts` only additively (a new optional filter parameter) if truly needed, with its own test, and record it in HANDOFF.
- Do not touch `supabase/` (no migrations, `9999_init.sql` may be frozen), `apps/web/vercel.json`, `proxy.ts`, or `next.config.ts` (3.4 changes headers). Do not build uploads (tus, `ResumableUpload`, `tus-js-client` dependency), share links, `/s/*`, `/embed/*`, announcements or bulletins.
- No new runtime dependencies (shadcn-generated components in `src/components/ui/*` are fine). Versions unchanged: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, TypeScript ~5.9 (never 7), ESLint 9 (never 10), Zod 4.5, supabase-js 2.112.
- Never expose whether a sermon exists to someone who cannot see it: missing or invisible rows → 404.
- Never `supabase db push` / `db reset`. No secrets or model identifiers in files or commits.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green; the new `apps/web` suites (`perms`, `player-strategy`, `dates`, `actions`, `LinkPreview`) run and pass.
- `pnpm --filter web build` with the mock env (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321 NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_ci_placeholder NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000`) → succeeds and the route list contains `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons`, `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/new`, `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/[id]`.
- `git grep -n "lib/supabase/service" apps/web/src/features/sermons` → nothing; `git grep -n "z.object" apps/web/src/features/sermons` → nothing; `git grep -n "youtube.com/embed" apps/web` → nothing (only `youtube-nocookie.com`, and only via the parser's `embedUrl`).
- If `apps/web/.env.local` points at a real Supabase project with the seed (or the founder's hosted project from step 2.5): sign in as a `sermons.link` holder, create a linked YouTube sermon from `https://youtu.be/<id>` and see the nocookie preview, publish it, open the detail page and play it, edit the title, unpublish to draft (disappears for a plain member), delete it with a `sermons.delete` account and confirm an `audit_log` row and (for uploads only) a `storage_deletions` row. Without a live project, record the manual script in `session_log.md` for the founder.
- Local DB cross-check (optional, no web needed): `scripts/db/local-up.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh && scripts/db/test.sh` still passes — you changed no SQL, so this proves your environment, not your code.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: in the feature table set Sermons → Web UI "list / link / edit / player / delete done; upload 3.3b; share 3.4"; State checklist: tick the sermons line partially ("3.3a done"); add under "Deviations from plan" anything you changed (additive query filter, forbidden-vs-notFound choice, any 1.7a signature that differed); add a note for 3.3b ("Upload tab placeholder in `NewSermonTabs.tsx`; incomplete-upload notice in `[id]/page.tsx`") and for 3.4 ("Share links placeholder card in `[id]/page.tsx`; `SermonPlayer` `variant: 'share'`").
- Tick step 3.3a in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(web): sermons list, linked sermons, edit, player, delete`; push `main` (`git push origin main`) unless another branch was named.
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.
done_when: `/o/<slug>/sermons` renders for an active member showing only published sermons, and for a `sermons.link`/`sermons.upload`/`sermons.delete` holder shows drafts and scheduled rows with status (published/drafts/scheduled/all), kind and search filters plus a 'New sermon' button.

`/o/<slug>/sermons/new` has Upload | Link tabs; the Link tab accepts a YouTube/Dropbox/Google Drive/other https URL, shows a live preview from `parseMediaLink(url,'web')` (YouTube renders a `youtube-nocookie.com` iframe; `http://` shows an error), and 'Publish now' / 'Schedule' / 'Save as draft' create a `sermons` row with `media_kind` = parsed kind, `external_url` = canonical URL and the chosen `publish_at`; the Upload tab is a disabled placeholder naming step 3.3b.

steps.title: Sermons — resumable upload (tus) with the 50 MB plan cap
steps.goal: The Upload tab of `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/new` works end to end for `sermons.upload` holders: the browser refuses files over the effective cap (min of `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` and the `sermon-media` bucket limit, 50 MB on Supabase Free) or outside the audio/video allow-list before any request; `planSermonUpload` inserts the `sermons` draft with the exact `sermonMediaPath` and the details; `ResumableUpload` drives `tus-js-client` against `${SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/upload/resumable` with the user's access token, 6 MiB chunks, `uploadDataDuringCreation`, `x-upsert: 'false'` and fingerprint resume; `finalizeSermonUpload` records size/MIME/probed duration and publishes or keeps a draft; Storage 413/415/409/401/403 responses map to clear messages that point at the Link tab; an interrupted upload shows an 'Upload incomplete' panel on the detail page with Finish / Resume / Discard. `docs/ENV.md` explains the two limits and how to raise them on Pro.

## Goal
When you finish, a leader holding `sermons.upload` can open the **Upload** tab of `/o/<slug>/sermons/new`, choose an audio or video file up to the church's upload limit (50 MB while Supabase is on the Free plan — `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB`), fill in the sermon details, and watch a resumable `tus-js-client` upload with progress, pause/resume and cancel. The flow is exactly PLAN §6: a Server Action inserts the `sermons` row with `publish_at = null` and the exact planned `storage_path`; the browser uploads to that path with the user's own access token; a second Server Action records size/MIME/duration and publishes (or leaves a draft). Files over the cap or of the wrong type are refused before any network call, and the Storage "exceeds plan limit"/MIME errors are mapped to clear messages that point at the Link tab. A draft whose upload never finished shows an "Upload incomplete" state on `/sermons/<id>` with resume, finish and discard options. Playback uses the `SermonPlayer` from 3.3a unchanged.

- Steps 3.1/2.1: `requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext`, `requirePerm(ctx, perm)`, `requireWritable(ctx)`, `ActionResult`/`ok`/`fail`, `toActionError`, `createServerSupabase()`, `createBrowserSupabase()`, `getSignedUrl(bucket, path, expiresIn)`, `publicEnv().supabaseUrl` (or the equivalent name 2.1a used — read `src/lib/env.ts`).
- Steps 1.6a/1.6b (`@church/domain`): `BUCKETS['sermon-media']` = `{ fileSizeLimitBytes, allowedMimeTypes }` parsed in parity with the migration's bucket row (50 MiB on Free); `MAX_UPLOAD_MB_DEFAULT = 50`; `readMaxUploadMb(raw)`; `sermonMediaPath(orgId, sermonId, uuid, ext)` → `${orgId}/sermons/${sermonId}/${uuid}.${ext}` (matches the `sermons_storage_path` check and the exact-path storage policy); `sermonUploadPlanSchemaFor(maxUploadMb)` — factory returning the Zod object `{ file_name, mime_type ∈ allowedMimeTypes, file_size_bytes ≤ min(maxUploadMb·1024·1024, fileSizeLimitBytes) }`; `mapStorageErrorMessage(message)` → a `DomainErrorKey` such as `file_too_large`, `unsupported_mime_type`, `object_already_exists` (read `packages/domain/src/errors.ts` for the exact keys); `sermonDetailsSchema`; `errorMessageFor(key)`.
- Step 1.7a (`@church/db`): `insertSermonDraft(db, { id, org_id, title, …, media_kind: 'upload', storage_path })` (caller supplies `id`), `updateSermonAfterUpload(db, id, { mime_type, file_size_bytes, duration_seconds })`, `publishSermon(db, id, publishAt)`, `deleteSermon(db, id)`, `getSermon(id)`.
- Database facts you build against (never edit `9999_init.sql`): `ca_sermons_insert_by_kind` lets `sermons.upload` holders insert `media_kind = 'upload'` rows when the org is writable; `sermons_media_shape` requires `storage_path` for uploads; `ca_storage_insert` on `storage.objects` calls `app.can_write_object(bucket_id, name)` = a `sermons` row exists whose `storage_path` **equals `name` exactly** and the caller holds `sermons.upload` — so the row MUST exist before the upload starts and the object name must be byte-identical to `storage_path`. There are **no update or delete policies** on `storage.objects` for `authenticated`: a failed or abandoned upload cannot be cleaned up by the browser; `srv_housekeeping()` (cron, step 3.6) deletes upload-kind draft rows older than 7 days that have no object, and the orphan sweep removes objects older than 24 h without a row. Quote this in the UI helper text.

## Build
1. **Dependency.** `pnpm --filter web add tus-js-client@<current 4.x>` (check with `npm view tus-js-client version`; never a major above 4; record the exact version in HANDOFF "Version pins worth remembering"). It is web-only — do not add it to the pnpm catalog.
2. **Effective cap** in `src/features/sermons/upload-limits.ts`: `effectiveUploadCapBytes()` = `Math.min(publicEnv().maxUploadMb * 1024 * 1024, BUCKETS['sermon-media'].fileSizeLimitBytes)`; `acceptAttribute()` = the `allowedMimeTypes` joined for `<input accept>` plus the extensions `.mp3,.m4a,.aac,.wav,.ogg,.mp4,.m4v,.mov,.webm`; `extensionAndMimeFor(file: File): { ext, mime } | null` — take the lowercase extension from the file name, map it to a canonical MIME (`mp3→audio/mpeg`, `m4a→audio/mp4`, `aac→audio/aac`, `wav→audio/wav`, `ogg→audio/ogg`, `mp4→video/mp4`, `m4v→video/mp4`, `mov→video/quicktime`, `webm→video/webm`); prefer `file.type` when it is non-empty AND in `allowedMimeTypes`, otherwise the mapped MIME (browsers on Windows often report an empty or generic type); return `null` when neither is allowed. Unit-test the table, including a `.MP3` uppercase name and an empty `file.type`.
3. **Server Actions** appended to `src/features/sermons/actions.ts` (same pipeline as 3.3a: `requireOrgMember(slug)` → `requirePerm(ctx, 'sermons.upload')` → `requireWritable(ctx)` → Zod → user client → `revalidatePath` → `ActionResult`):
   - `planSermonUpload(slug, { file_name, mime_type, file_size_bytes, details })`: parse `sermonUploadPlanSchemaFor(publicEnv().maxUploadMb)` and `sermonDetailsSchema` (details are saved now so a crash mid-upload loses nothing but the file); a `file_size_bytes` over the cap fails with key `file_too_large` and a message that names the limit in MB and the Link tab; `id = crypto.randomUUID()`, `objectId = crypto.randomUUID()`, `ext` from `file_name` (validated against the table in item 2), `storage_path = sermonMediaPath(ctx.org.orgId, id, objectId, ext)`; `insertSermonDraft(db, { id, org_id, media_kind: 'upload', storage_path, mime_type, …details })` (leave `file_size_bytes`, `duration_seconds` null, `publish_at` null regardless of the chosen publish state — publishing happens in finalize); return `{ sermonId: id, storagePath: storage_path, bucket: 'sermon-media' }`.
   - `finalizeSermonUpload(slug, { sermonId, mime_type, file_size_bytes, duration_seconds, publish: 'now' | 'schedule' | 'draft', publish_at? })`: `getSermon(sermonId)` → 404 if missing or not `media_kind = 'upload'`; `updateSermonAfterUpload(db, sermonId, { mime_type, file_size_bytes, duration_seconds })`; then `publishSermon(db, sermonId, now | publish_at | null)`; return `{ id }`. It is idempotent: calling it twice with the same values is harmless.
   - `discardSermonUpload(slug, { sermonId })`: only for rows with `media_kind = 'upload' and publish_at is null and file_size_bytes is null`; requires `sermons.delete` (`deleteSermon` is governed by the delete policy — an uploader without `sermons.delete` cannot remove their own draft; the UI explains that housekeeping removes abandoned drafts after 7 days). If the caller lacks `sermons.delete` return `permission_denied`.
   - `checkSermonObject(slug, { sermonId })`: for the incomplete state — `db.storage.from('sermon-media').list(dirname(storage_path))` with the user client (the select policy permits listing objects the caller may read) and return `{ exists, size, mimetype }` for the object named `basename(storage_path)`, or `{ exists: false }` on any error.
4. **`upload-client.ts`** (`src/features/sermons/upload-client.ts`, browser-only, no React): `startTusUpload({ file, bucket, objectName, contentType, supabaseUrl, getAccessToken, onProgress(bytes, total), onSuccess(), onError(err) , onShouldRetry? }) → { pause(), resume(), abort() }`. Configure `new tus.Upload(file, …)` exactly per DESIGN §7: `endpoint: `${supabaseUrl}/storage/v1/upload/resumable``, `chunkSize: 6 * 1024 * 1024` (Supabase requires 6 MiB chunks), `uploadDataDuringCreation: true`, `removeFingerprintOnSuccess: true`, `retryDelays: [0, 3000, 5000, 10000, 20000]`, headers `{ authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`, 'x-upsert': 'false' }`, metadata `{ bucketName: bucket, objectName, contentType, cacheControl: '3600' }`. Before `upload.start()` call `upload.findPreviousUploads()` and `resumeFromPreviousUpload` when one matches (this is what makes "Resume" work after a reload). Fetch the access token lazily via `getAccessToken` (`(await createBrowserSupabase().auth.getSession()).data.session?.access_token`) so a refreshed token is used; on a 401 response refresh once (`auth.refreshSession()`), update the header and `start()` again. Wrap tus in this module so it can be unit-tested with `vi.mock('tus-js-client')`.
5. **`upload-errors.ts`**: `uploadErrorToKey(err): DomainErrorKey` — read the HTTP status from tus's `DetailedError` (`err.originalResponse?.getStatus()`) and the body: 413 or a body matching `mapStorageErrorMessage` → `file_too_large` ("This file is larger than the current upload limit (<N> MB on the church's Supabase plan). Upload a smaller file or link a recording on YouTube (unlisted), Dropbox or Google Drive."); 415 / "mime type … not supported" → `unsupported_mime_type`; 409 / "already exists" → `object_already_exists` ("This file already finished uploading — click Finish."); 401 → `auth_required` ("Your session expired — sign in again and resume."); 403 → `permission_denied` ("You no longer have permission to upload sermons, or the church is suspended."); network/timeout → `network_error` ("Connection lost — the upload will resume when you retry."). Table-test it with fake responses. Reuse `errorMessageFor` where the catalogue already has copy; only the file-size message is computed (needs the number).
6. **`ResumableUpload.tsx`** (client): props `{ file, plan: { sermonId, storagePath, bucket }, contentType, onDone(result), onError(key) }`; renders a progress bar (`Progress` from shadcn), bytes/percent, an estimated remaining time (simple moving average), and buttons Pause / Resume / Cancel. Cancel calls `abort()` then `onError('cancelled')`. Warn on `beforeunload` while uploading ("Your upload is still running").
7. **`UploadSermonForm.tsx`** (client) replaces the placeholder in `NewSermonTabs.tsx`: a `FileDropzone` (`<input type="file" accept={acceptAttribute()}>` + drag-and-drop) that validates immediately with `extensionAndMimeFor` and `effectiveUploadCapBytes()` — a too-large or wrong-type file is refused with the mapped message before any request; shows name, size, and "Maximum file size: <N> MB (Supabase Free plan). Longer recordings: host them on YouTube (unlisted), Dropbox or Google Drive and use the Link tab." Then the `SermonForm` fields (`mode: 'create'`). Submit sequence: (a) `probeMediaDuration(file)` (item 8) in parallel with (b) `planSermonUpload` → (c) `ResumableUpload` to `plan.storagePath` → (d) `finalizeSermonUpload` with the real `file.size`, the canonical MIME and the probed duration → redirect to `/o/<slug>/sermons/<id>` with a success toast. If (c) fails after the row exists, keep the page, show the mapped error and offer Retry (same plan, tus resumes) or "Discard draft" (only when `canDeleteSermon(ctx)`), and tell the user the draft is visible under Drafts as "Upload incomplete". Disable the submit button while running; double-submit must not create two rows.
8. **`probeMediaDuration(file): Promise<number | null>`** in `src/features/sermons/media-probe.ts`: create an `<audio>` or `<video>` element by MIME, `src = URL.createObjectURL(file)`, resolve `Math.round(duration)` on `loadedmetadata`, `null` on `error` or after a 5-second timeout, always `revokeObjectURL`. Infinity/NaN → null.
9. **Incomplete-upload state** on `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/[id]` (replace 3.3a's notice with `IncompleteUploadPanel.tsx`): explain what happened; button **Finish** (runs `checkSermonObject`; if the object exists, call `finalizeSermonUpload` with its size/mimetype and `publish: 'draft'` so the leader can publish from the form); button **Resume** (file picker: accept the same file — require identical `size` and compatible MIME, then run `ResumableUpload` to the existing `storage_path`; tus resumes if a fingerprint exists, otherwise starts the object anew — allowed because the object does not exist yet); button **Discard** (`discardSermonUpload`; disabled with tooltip "Needs the Delete sermons permission — abandoned drafts are removed automatically after 7 days" when the visitor lacks `sermons.delete`). Members never reach this state (drafts are invisible to them).
10. **List page**: 3.3a's status badge gains "Upload incomplete" for upload drafts with `file_size_bytes is null`.
11. **Tests** (2.1a harness, jsdom): `upload-limits.test.ts` (cap = min(env, bucket) — with `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=200` the cap is still the bucket's 50 MiB; MIME/extension table); `upload-errors.test.ts` (each branch); `upload-client.test.ts` with `vi.mock('tus-js-client')` asserting endpoint, `chunkSize` 6 MiB, `uploadDataDuringCreation: true`, `x-upsert: 'false'`, metadata keys `bucketName/objectName/contentType/cacheControl`, that `findPreviousUploads` is consulted, and that a 401 triggers one refresh + restart; `actions.test.ts` additions with a mocked user client — `planSermonUpload` rejects 50 MiB + 1 byte with `file_too_large` and never calls `insertSermonDraft`, rejects `audio/x-unknown`, inserts `storage_path` matching `^<org>/sermons/<id>/[0-9a-f-]{36}\.mp3$` with `publish_at` null even when the user chose "Publish now"; `finalizeSermonUpload` publishes only then; `discardSermonUpload` needs `sermons.delete`; `media-probe.test.ts` resolves null on timeout (fake timers).
12. **Docs**: add a section "Sermon uploads" to `docs/ENV.md` next to `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` explaining the two limits (env cap and the bucket `file_size_limit`, the effective cap is the smaller), how to raise both when the project moves to Supabase Pro (Vercel env + a `9998_*` bucket upsert paste — never edit the frozen `9999_init.sql`), and that abandoned drafts/objects are cleaned by the step 3.6 cron.

## Constraints
- The browser uploads with the **user's** access token only; the service client is never imported by `src/features/sermons/*`. `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and the publishable key are the only Supabase values in client code.
- The object name must equal the inserted `storage_path` byte for byte (exact-path policy) — never build the path in two places; both come from `sermonMediaPath`. `x-upsert` stays `'false'`.
- Keep `chunkSize` at exactly 6 MiB (`6 * 1024 * 1024`) — Supabase's resumable endpoint rejects other sizes.
- Do not change `SermonPlayer`, `player-strategy.ts` or the Link tab beyond wiring; do not touch `supabase/`, `next.config.ts`, `proxy.ts`, `apps/web/vercel.json`. No share links, `/s/*`, `/embed/*`, announcements or bulletins.
- Versions unchanged (Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, TS ~5.9 not 7, ESLint 9 not 10); only new dependency `tus-js-client` 4.x in `apps/web`.
- Never `supabase db push` / `db reset`. No secrets or model identifiers anywhere.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green including the new suites (`upload-limits`, `upload-errors`, `upload-client`, `media-probe`, `actions` additions).
- `pnpm --filter web build` with the mock env → succeeds; `grep -c "tus-js-client" apps/web/package.json` → `1`; `git grep -n "tus-js-client" pnpm-workspace.yaml` → nothing (not in the catalog).
- `git grep -n "6 \* 1024 \* 1024" apps/web/src/features/sermons/upload-client.ts` → 1 hit; `git grep -n "x-upsert" apps/web/src` → only `upload-client.ts` with `'false'`; `git grep -n "lib/supabase/service" apps/web/src/features/sermons` → nothing.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are inlined at build time, so do not test the cap by exporting env at runtime — the `upload-limits.test.ts` case (env 200 MB, bucket 50 MiB → cap 50 MiB) is the proof that the bucket limit wins.
- With a live project (`apps/web/.env.local` from the founder's step 2.5 project, or the seed): as a `sermons.upload` holder upload a ~1 MB mp3 → row appears as Draft → progress reaches 100 % → finalize publishes → the detail page plays it through the signed URL; try a 51 MB file → refused client-side with the limit message; temporarily set `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=60` locally and try a 55 MB file → the Storage 413 is mapped to the `file_too_large` message (bucket wins); reload mid-upload → "Upload incomplete" → Resume with the same file completes. Without a live project, write this script into `session_log.md` for the founder's acceptance run (step 3.9).

steps.notes: Second half of the 3.3 split. Key constraint from the schema: `storage.objects` has no update/delete policy for `authenticated`, so a browser can neither replace nor remove an object — hence `x-upsert: 'false'`, the row-before-upload ordering, and the reliance on `srv_housekeeping` (7-day draft purge) and the cron orphan sweep (3.6) for abandoned uploads; `discardSermonUpload` needs `sermons.delete` because the row delete policy demands it (an uploader without that permission cannot delete their own draft — documented default). Sermon details are saved at plan time (before the upload) so a crash loses only the file; DESIGN's wording 'update size/mime/duration → set publish_at' is honoured in `finalizeSermonUpload`. Duration is probed client-side (best effort, null when the browser cannot decode). `tus-js-client` 4.x is the only new dependency; Supabase's resumable endpoint requires exactly 6 MiB chunks. Error keys `file_too_large`, `unsupported_mime_type`, `object_already_exists`, `network_error` must match `packages/domain/src/errors.ts` from 1.6b — if that catalogue used different names the agent adopts them (open issue for the assembler).

steps.title: Share links + /s/[token] + /embed/yt/[id]
steps.goal: Leaders holding `sermons.link` or `sermons.upload` manage public share links from a `ShareLinksPanel` on `/o/[orgSlug]/sermons/[id]` (create via `create_share_link` with label, password ≥ 8 — mandatory when `sermon_share_requires_password` — expiry and max views; the `${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/s/<token>` URL is shown exactly once; list with status and `view_count`; revoke). `POST /api/share/<token>/unlock` with the right password sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, `Path=/s/<token>`, 24-hour jose-signed cookie and redirects 303 to `/s/<token>`; a wrong password redirects with `?error=wrong_password` and no cookie; a visitor with a valid cookie is served without re-entering the password, and revoking the link or disabling sharing makes the next visit a 404 even with the cookie.

The unlocked page plays uploaded media through a 1-hour signed URL in `SermonPlayer` (`variant: 'share'`) and shows a Download button ONLY when `allow_download` is true (i.e. `sermon_share_allow_download` on and `media_kind = 'upload'`), using a signed URL with attachment disposition; external sermons render the nocookie YouTube iframe / Drive preview / native stream plus an always-present 'Open at provider' link and never a download control.

Responses for `/s/*` carry `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and a CSP with `frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://drive.google.com`; `/embed/yt/<11-char id>` returns 200 without `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`, with noindex, and renders a full-viewport `youtube-nocookie.com/embed/<id>` iframe; `/embed/yt/<bad id>` is 404.

Unit suites for `src/lib/share/token.ts` (hash vector, 43-char base64url validation, IP header precedence), `src/lib/share/cookie.ts` (roundtrip, tamper, expiry, wrong secret, token-hash mismatch, missing secret), `resolve.ts` (status mapping, cookie-path row validator), the unlock route, `share-actions.ts`, security headers and `SharePage` pass; `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` and `pnpm --filter web build` (mock env) are green; `curl -sI /s/unknown` → 404 with the headers above.

HANDOFF.md ticks share links, records the deviations (token-derived cookie name, TypeScript re-validation for cookie visits with a proposed `srv_load_share_link`, unlock route path, `media-src https:`), the `jose` version and the founder to-do that `SHARE_LINK_COOKIE_SECRET` must exist in Vercel; docs/TODO.md step 3.4 is ticked.

Signed URLs and provider links stay reachable for up to 1 hour after revocation — surfaced in the Revoke dialog. open_issues: Skeleton step 3.3 was split into 3.3a (list, linked sermons, edit, player, delete) and 3.3b (tus upload). 3.4 `depends_on` is `3.3b`; any other group that referenced `3.3` (3.7 Web QA in G10, 4.2 mobile playback in G11) should be repointed to `3.3b` (or `3.3a` when only `SermonPlayer` is needed) at assembly.

Unlock cookie name: DESIGN §7 says `share_{linkId}`, but 1.6b left `link_id` OPTIONAL on `needs_password` results because the 1.3b RPC may not return it. 3.4 derives the cookie name from the token hash (`share_<first 16 hex>`) and records the deviation. If the assembler confirms 1.3b returns `link_id` on `needs_password`, the prompt can revert to `share_{linkId}`.

Cookie-verified share visits: `srv_resolve_share_link` returns the `ok` payload only with the password, so 3.4 re-reads and re-validates the rows in TypeScript via the service client (`loadUnlockedShare`). Proposed step 3.11 moves this into a `9998_*` migration; if adopted, Phase 2's `9998_join_codes.sql` (5.6) and Phase 3's `9997_surveys_head_of_house.sql` (6.1) must be renumbered down by one.

Unlock route path: PLAN §7/§8 say `/api/share/[token]/unlock`, DESIGN §9 draws `app/(public)/s/[token]/unlock/route.ts`. 3.4 follows PLAN (decision 10) and asks the agent to add `/api/share/*` to the `proxy.ts` matcher exclusions; G5 (2.1a) listed only `/s/*` and `/embed/*`.

Referrer policy: PLAN §6 / DESIGN §7 prescribe `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on `/s/*`, which would also strip the referer from the YouTube/Drive iframes on the share page. 3.4 keeps the header and sets `referrerPolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"` on the iframe elements (3.3a does the same in `SermonPlayer`); `/embed/*` uses `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` because it exists to supply a referer to YouTube. The docs could be updated to say so.

CSP `media-src`: DESIGN §9 lists only the Supabase host, but Dropbox (`dl.dropboxusercontent.com`) and 'other https' native streams need `media-src https:` on both the admin pages and `/s/*`. 3.4 widens it for `/s/*`; G5's 2.1a CSP for the `(org)` pages may need the same widening for 3.3a's admin player — flagged for the assembler (3.3a is told not to edit `next.config.ts`).

`requirePerm(ctx, perm)` from 3.1 takes a single key; share links need `sermons.link` OR `sermons.upload`. 3.4 adds `requireAnyPerm(ctx, perms[])` in `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts` if G7 did not already provide one — G7's 3.1 prompt should be checked at assembly.

Uploaders without `sermons.delete` cannot discard their own incomplete upload draft (row delete policy requires `sermons.delete`); 3.3b documents reliance on `srv_housekeeping` (7-day draft purge) and the cron orphan sweep (3.6).
